exclusions_stated_by_publisher: Feed publishes one row per incident coded to HIGHEST_NIBRS_CODE (the single highest-severity NIBRS offense per incident); lower-ranked offenses in the same incident are not published as rows (evidence/README.md lines 25-27, 114-120; evidence/01_fetch_charlotte.py lines 13-15).
Source coverage per metadata: DATE_REPORTED from 2017-01-01 to current (evidence/README.md lines 9-11).
known_differences_from_fetch_script: Block-group handling: the script left-joins to tl_2020_37_bg with predicate within, drops the 5 rows with no block-group match (all near the airport), and keeps the first row per incident_id after the join (evidence/01_fetch_charlotte.py lines 186-196; evidence/README.md lines 89-96). The contract joins with within to state 37 block groups; if the runner keeps unmatched points or does not re-dedupe after the join, its row count before the BG step is 267,756 vs the script's 267,751 in incidents_bg.parquet.

Year: the script derives year from DATE_REPORTED parsed as epoch ms in UTC (lines 144, 165-167). The contract uses date_field DATE_REPORTED with epoch_ms. All 267,756 DATE_REPORTED values in raw_cache.parquet are local midnight stored as 04:00 or 05:00 UTC (177,708 and 90,048 rows), so the UTC year equals the local year; the YEAR column also equals that year in all 267,756 rows (recomputed from raw_cache.parquet), so year_field YEAR would give the same result.

Coordinates: the script takes latitude/longitude from the feature geometry requested with outSR=4326 (lines 101, 124-126). The contract reads latitude|__arcgis_latitude and longitude|__arcgis_longitude; a live pull reproduces the script only if the runner also requests WGS84 (outSR=4326) geometry.

Case sensitivity: the script's OFFENSE_MAP lookup is an exact pandas .map (line 152); the rules set case_sensitive true to match. The 14 distinct HIGHEST_NIBRS_CODE values in the archived pull are all exact whitelist codes (evidence/raw_cache_profile.json), so case-insensitive matching would give the same rows.

Where clause: the script's ArcGIS where uses fixed bounds timestamp '2018-01-01 00:00:00' / '2025-01-01 00:00:00' (lines 77-82); the contract writes them as {start}/{end} in the same ArcGIS timestamp literal syntax, not the ISO 'T' form.

Output columns: the script renames and passes through DIVISION_ID, CMPD_PATROL_DIVISION, NPA, CITY, ZIP, ADDRESS_DESCRIPTION, HIGHEST_NIBRS_CODE, HIGHEST_NIBRS_DESCRIPTION into incidents_bg.parquet (lines 200-214) and writes offense_mapping.csv and a summary pivot; the contract does not express output column naming.
The script adds a computed DATE_REPORTED_utc column to raw_cache.parquet (line 144); the contract does not need or produce it.
notes: Recomputed from raw_cache.parquet (267,756 rows): 0 rows with HIGHEST_NIBRS_CODE outside the 14-code whitelist (profile distinct counts sum to 267,756: larceny 23A-23H = 62,500+53,978+38,514+10,801+6,753+1,092+886+220 = 174,744; 240 = 31,349; 220 = 28,992; 13A = 19,635; 120 = 10,751; 11A = 1,656; 09A = 629), 0 null or (0,0) coordinates, 0 duplicate or null INCIDENT_REPORT_ID, 0 rows whose UTC year of DATE_REPORTED is outside 2018-2024 (2018 37,804; 2019 39,899; 2020 35,568; 2021 34,541; 2022 36,814; 2023 42,087; 2024 41,043). So the contract keeps all 267,756 rows before the block-group join, matching the script's pre-join count; the script's final 267,751 reflects its drop of 5 BG-unmatched rows (README lines 89-96). Jurisdictions: CMPD is described as county-wide, policing Charlotte and unincorporated Mecklenburg County plus 'several small incorporated towns' that the README does not name (README lines 13-23, 105-109). I listed Charlotte city (266,009 incidents in jurisdictions.csv) and the NC nonmunicipal remainder (39,154; unincorporated Mecklenburg; note this id is statewide, not Mecklenburg-only). I left out Mint Hill (3,636), Matthews (1,788), Huntersville (566), Pineville (396), Davidson (8), and the out-of-county Stallings (9, Union) and Concord (3, Cabarrus). Reasons: the jurisdictions.csv counts sum to 311,569, more than the 267,756 rows, so they overlap (they look like block-group-level assignment) and do not show point-level service. The raw fields also show little town activity: CITY = MATTHEWS 70, PINEVILLE 42, HUNTERSVILLE 32, MINT HILL 9 rows over 7 years, and the town-coded DIVISION_IDs MA 47 / PI 25 / MI 9 all have CMPD_PATROL_DIVISION 'NA'. That is not what full primary-agency coverage of those towns would produce. The evidence does not settle the town question. To settle it, we need a publisher statement of CMPD's service area (which Mecklenburg towns, if any, contract CMPD as primary agency, e.g. Huntersville division 92, 93 rows, and Davidson division 90, 3 rows) or a point-in-place count of incidents in each town. A reviewer should confirm before this list is final.
